name: Carlos Romero-Barceló
bio: a Resident Commissioner from Puerto Rico; born in San Juan, P.R., September 4, 1932; graduated from Phillips Exeter Academy, Exeter, N.H., 1949; B.A., Yale University, 1953; LL.B., University of Puerto Rico School of Law, 1956; practicing attorney, San Juan; mayor of San Juan, 1969-1976; member, board of directors, U.S. Conference of Mayors and National League of Cities, 1976; president, National League of Cities, 1976; president, New Progressive Party, 1974-1985 and 1989-1992; Governor of Puerto Rico, 1977-1985; chairman, Southern Governors Association, 1980-1981; member of the Puerto Rico senate, 1986-1989; elected as a New Progressive to the One Hundred Third Congress for a four-year term and reelected to the succeeding term (January 3, 1993-January 3, 2001); caucused with the Democratic Party; unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the One Hundred Seventh Congress in 2000; died on May 2, 2021, in San Juan, P.R.; lay in state in La Fortaleza in San Juan, P.R., May 6, 2021; remains were cremated.
